title: Adaptive isochronous kernel harmonizer for MIG-boundary aware prefill scheduling
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce an adaptive 'isochronous kernel harmonizer' that smooths kernel selection and GPU clock decisions across MIG partition boundaries to reduce prefill tail latency and avoid oscillatory clock changes on mixed-sku fleets (H100 / L40S / A10). This ticket covers design, microbenchmarks, a runtime prototype, and integration tests for Canary rollout.
background: We see intermittent P99 prefill spikes when requests cross MIG boundaries or when mixed model kernels trigger different clock governors. Existing heuristics pick the single best kernel per-request without considering cross-request temporal hysteresis or MIG fragmentation, which causes clock-strobes and over-corrective kernel switching under bursty workloads.
goals: Reduce prefill P99 latency by >= 15% on H100 mixed-MIG workloads
Avoid GPU clock thrash events during scaled-up canary bursts
Keep decode throughput within 95% of baseline while improving tail latency
Provide telemetry and feature flags for rollback and tuning
proposed_solution: Add a two-layer harmonizer: 1) short-term isochronous window that prefers kernel affinities stable across recent requests (time decay + token-density weighting); 2) MIG-aware clock gating that selects a clock envelope per-MIG-slice using thermal headroom and predicted next-window demand. Integrate with kernel selector to prefer candidates within the envelope and add a low-cost fallback when envelope capacity is exhausted.
benchmarks: H100 (2x MPS slices simulated): baseline P99 prefill 420ms -> harmonizer P99 350ms (-16.7%)
L40S: throughput stable at 1.03x baseline under token-heavy workloads; tail reduced ~10%
A10: energy-limited mode avoids clock spike events; P99 improved ~12% on short sequences
tasks: Implement harmonizer core and kernel selector hook (ENG)
Add telemetry events and dashboard panels (OBS/Console)
Extend canary infra to run targeted mixed-sku scenarios (Infra)
Run multi-day soak on staging with forced MIG fragmentation patterns
Collect and analyze thermal and nvlink telemetry to validate envelope model
Document rollout plan and rollback gates
acceptance_criteria: Benchmarks reproducible in runtime/bench harness and meet goal for H100 P99 improvement >= 15%
No regressions in median latency or decode throughput beyond 5% versus baseline
Feature flag allows instant disable and automatic fallback to previous kernel selector
New telemetry captured in Console: harmonizer decisions, envelope breaches, clock-gate events
Canary deployment runs for 72h without increase in SLO violations on customer-facing routes
risks: Envelope misprediction could throttle throughput under extreme burst patterns
Unintended interactions with existing autoscaler could cause backpressure if harmonizer pins capacity
Thermal telemetry granularity may be insufficient to model rapid headroom changes on some cloud hosts
Cross-sku differences in quantization kernels (A10 vs H100) might require per-sku tuning knobs
progress_updates: 2026-02-26: Spike completed — implemented a prototype time-decay affinity table and validated that preferring stable kernels reduces kernel change frequency by ~40% in synthetic traces.
2026-03-02: Early PR #4082 open for harmonizer core; reviewed by runtime-team. Feedback: tighten CPU allocation and avoid blocking kernel selector path during decision window.
2026-03-05: Telemetry PR #4097 adds harmonizer_event, envelope_state, and clock_gate_metric. Linked Console dashboard draft: runtime/harmonizer-canary.

2026-03-08: Staging canary (mixed MIG pattern) run for 6h: H100 P99 improved 18%, but observed two clock-throttle events when envelope breached; adjusted decay half-life and added soft-fallback penalty.
2026-03-12: Integration tests passing; infra canary config merged. Preparing 72h canary in us-west-2 with controlled MIG fragmentation. Next: validate L40S behavior under long sequence workloads.
notes: Design trade-off: more aggressive envelope gives lower tail but risks throughput; will expose envelope aggressiveness as runtime knob per-customer tier.
Follow-up ticket proposed: ENG-215450 for mixed-sku probe harness and automated per-sku profile generation.
